headline: Red Sox explode in extras to keep the good times rolling
morning_brew: I was staring at the screen, ready to throw my remote through the wall, until that eleventh inning saved my sanity. Putting up seven runs is a damn statement, and watching us lock down the late innings like a vault was exactly what the doctor ordered. Those four runs late in the game finally let me unclench my jaw for the first time since the first pitch. It feels like this squad is actually starting to click, which is a hell of a relief after the torture we have endured all summer long.

Tolle gave us a gutsy start and kept the opposition quiet for a long stretch. The bullpen did the heavy lifting late, and honestly, watching that group navigate the traffic without folding was a total shock to the system. I spent most of the middle innings pacing my kitchen like a caged animal, but the way Gamboa and E.E. Miller handled those high-leverage spots should give us all a bit more confidence. Even my neighbor Rick, who usually has a folder full of conspiracy theories about the league sabotaging our every move, finally put his pencil down and admitted the pitching staff looked sharp.

We have another date with the Marlins tonight before we pack up for a trip to New York to face the Yankees. Staying in the win column is all that matters, and keeping the focus on the task at hand is exactly what I want to see. I am not looking ahead to the weekend just yet, but piling up victories is the best way to keep the pressure on in the division. The Duck Boat fund is getting a nice little boost this week, so let's keep the pedal to the floor.
